C45223.observed: What was checked: which bin the system chooses for you when you pick a part, and whether it ever spreads the quantity across bins on its own. What happened, using a part whose default bin holds 6. Asking for 2 - which the default bin comfortably covers - put the whole 2 on the default bin. Asking for 50 - which no bin holds - left the allocation on the default bin anyway rather than moving it somewhere else or giving up. In neither case did the system split the quantity between bins by itself: the chip always names one bin, never a number of them. So it makes a sensible single choice and leaves any splitting to the user.
C45223.not_observed: The middle case - where the default bin is short but some other single bin does cover the quantity - could not be checked: every stocked part on this branch is held in one bin only, so there is no other bin to move to.

C45231.observed: What was checked: whether changing the quantity after the bin has been chosen makes the system think again. What happened: with the bin chosen automatically, the quantity was changed and the allocation was worked out again each time. At 5 - still within the 6 the bin holds - nothing was flagged. At 50 the warning appeared straight away and used the new number: "Only 6 here. Pulling 50 takes this bin negative." So the allocation is not left stale against an old quantity.
C45231.not_observed: The other half - that a bin you chose BY HAND is kept rather than re-picked when the quantity changes - could not be checked here: every stocked part on this branch sits in a single bin, so there is no second bin to choose by hand.

C45238.observed: What was checked: whether the bin chip can be reached with the keyboard, and where it sits in the order. What happened: tabbing forward from the Qty box went Qty, then Save, then Cancel, then the "Pulled from" bin chip - and the next Tab wrapped back round into the row. So the chip is reachable without the mouse and it is the last stop in the row, after both buttons, which is where the case says it should be.

C45242.observed: What was checked: that the system does not explain itself when there is nothing to explain. What happened: a quantity of 2 was asked for from a default bin holding 6 - so the default bin covers it and no switching was needed. No note appeared beside the chip at all. The explanation only shows up when the system has actually moved the allocation somewhere the user did not choose.
